- **Parallel destination (`crime_00003`) — Warn.** `/admin/billing-plans` and `/billing-plans` appear to represent the same intent, but confidence is only `0.6`; the split could be deliberate. Require the PR to identify the canonical route and either redirect the duplicate or document why both exist. The orphan findings for both routes strengthen the warning.

- **Command/docs drift (`crime_00013`) — Warn.** Docs advertise `iaq teams`, `iaq workspace`, and `iaq refresh`, while the bin exposes only `get` and `list`. This is highly credible (`0.8`) and guarantees failed commands, but it is lower-impact than an access-policy inconsistency. Update the docs or restore the commands. I would not ignore it.

The **parallel destination carries the highest computed agent-risk: `0.33`**, versus `0.25` for permission drift and `0.19` for command drift. An agent can confidently update one billing flow while entirely missing its unlinked twin; both routes are also orphaned, so there is no navigation, documentation, or import trail revealing their relationship. Permission drift is the stronger merge blocker because of its authorization implications, even though its modelled agent-risk score is lower.
